sections.label: Greatest crisis faced by Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore is in the greatest crisis it has ever faced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We are in the midst of the greatest crisis ever faced by Singapore.

sections.label: COVID-19 and tighter finances
sections.summary: After 55 years of prosperity, the COVID-19 pandemic has left Singapore in a very serious situation with tighter financial resources ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore has prospered over the past 55 years, but the COVID-19 pandemic has put us in a very serious situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moving ahead, our country’s financial resources will certainly be much tighter.

sections.label: Loneliness among older Singaporeans
sections.summary: A Duke-NUS study of 4,500 Singaporeans aged 60 and above found 34% reported being sometimes or mostly lonely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a study by Duke-NUS on 4,500 Singaporeans aged 60 and above, 34% reported that they were sometimes or mostly lonely.

sections.label: HDB Proximity Housing Grant
sections.summary: HDB provides the Proximity Housing Grant to help families buy a resale flat to live with or close to each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, HDB provides the Proximity Housing Grant to help families buy a resale flat to live with or close to each other for mutual care and support.

sections.label: Local programmes for seniors
sections.summary: Grassroots leaders should organise local efforts using Community Networks for Seniors and SG Cares to offer active ageing, befriending and care programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Include the grassroots leaders, organise it at the local level, leverage on the work of the Community Networks for Seniors and SG Cares, and offer active ageing, befriending and care programmes for our seniors.

sections.label: Intergenerational programmes and services
sections.summary: More intergenerational programmes can let the young care for the old and the old mentor the young, including at the new Yio Chu Kang Community Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One way is to improve on and have more intergenerational programmes and services – where the young can take care of the old, and for the old to mentor the young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, senior volunteers mentoring at-risk primary school children from low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There will be a chance for us to do so in the new Yio Chu Kang Community Centre.

sections.label: Yio Chu Kang kampong spirit
sections.summary: Some former residents still live in Yio Chu Kang today, and the old kampong spirit should be rebuilt and carried over for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some are still living in Yio Chu Kang today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We should rebuild and carry-over the old kampong spirit for Singapore.

sections.label: Movement skills window of opportunity
sections.summary: Ages four to seven are called the window of opportunity, when children who pick up fundamental movement skills grow more confident and stay active and healthy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From a motor development perspective, the age between four and seven is often termed as the "window of opportunity".

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Children who pick up fundamental movement skills during this critical period grow to be more confident, have higher self-esteem and maintain an active and healthy lifestyle throughout their lives.

sections.label: Mandatory preschool education proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges higher standards and suggests preschool education become mandatory for all Singaporean children to combat inequality early and give every child opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While the Government has been forthcoming in its support for early childhood education, I urge us to hold ourselves to a higher standard and would like to suggest that preschool education become mandatory for all Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mandating compulsory preschool education underlies our strong commitment in combating inequality at the earliest juncture possible and ensures that every Singaporean child is given the opportunity, the opportunity to discover the joy of exploration and play and, importantly, they stand a chance, just a chance when they enter primary school.

sections.label: Broad Industry 4.0 skills
sections.summary: Emphasising broad Industry 4.0 skills generalisable across disciplines can better position fresh graduates and give them confidence to apply technical skills in other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On the other hand, an emphasis on broad skills rooted in Industry 4.0 that can be generalised across other disciplines can put our fresh graduates on a better footing and give them the confidence to apply their technical skills across other relevant sectors.

sections.label: Four-and-a-half-day work week training
sections.summary: The speaker hopes all workers can one day take courses to reinvent themselves, possibly via a four-and-a-half-day work week with the half day for skills training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With that, I hope that we are able to one day provide all our workers the opportunity to undertake courses to reinvent themselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This may mean encouraging the move towards a four-and-a-half-day work week, with the remainder half day dedicated for skills training.

sections.label: Government support for compulsory preschool
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government can make preschool education compulsory for Singaporean children and provide the necessary support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As such, I hope that the Government can make preschool education compulsory for Singaporean children and provide the necessary support and so on.

sections.label: Asatizah adaptation and education vision
sections.summary: The speaker hopes religious teachers adapt through COFA and shares a vision of extended education from early childhood to polytechnic and university review.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They have proven to be good role models in terms of adaptation and lifelong learning, and I hope that our community will also follow their footsteps.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I believe in their capabilities, and I hope that existing religious teachers and those who have just returned home, can continue to adapt to the current context through the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) and reinvent themselves in various fields and disciplines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, in summary, I had shared my vision of an extended education system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is one that begins with mandatory early childhood education to ensure that no child is left behind, followed by a review of our polytechnic and university courses, so that it is streamlined and focused on providing our graduates with a strong general foundation so that they remain agile in a volatile world.

sections.label: Online concert ticket sales
sections.summary: A physical concert with limited capacity became an online concert that sold 750,000 tickets, equal to 15 normal concerts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They transformed a physical concert with limited capacity into an online concert with limitless reach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This breakthrough in thinking resulted in the concert selling 750,000 tickets, which is equivalent to holding 15 concerts in normal times.

sections.label: Concurrent paid viewers peak
sections.summary: The show reached a peak of 756,000 concurrent paid viewers in 107 countries and territories.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The show reached a peak of 756,000 concurrent paid viewers in 107 countries and territories.

sections.label: BTS concert viewership equivalent
sections.summary: The BTS concert's paid viewership equalled 15 shows at a 50,000-seat stadium, but was streamed from a smaller Seoul studio.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The BTS concert’s paid viewership was the equivalent to 15 shows at a 50,000-seat stadium, but the concert was streamed from a much smaller venue, a studio in Seoul.

sections.label: SIRS helped 180,000 people
sections.summary: Thirteen years later, about 180,000 people have been helped by SIRS, including arts freelancers and various other workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Thirteen years later today, some 180,000 people have been helped by SIRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Besides arts freelancers, it has helped sports coaches, taxi and private hire car drivers, food delivery riders, tourist guides, home bakers and many others making different livelihoods.

sections.label: CPF-based support schemes
sections.summary: Many Government support schemes like WIS are based on CPF contributions, so SEPs who do not contribute will not qualify easily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Many Government support schemes, like the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), are based on CPF contributions and, inevitably, SEPs who do not contribute will not qualify easily.

sections.label: CPF contributions for SEPs
sections.summary: The speaker applauds MOM's CAYE pilot for SEP MediSave contributions and calls for more explanation and incentives for SEPs to contribute to CPF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: There is, naturally, a high inertia for them coming on board the CPF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: So, I applaud the MOM for piloting the Contribute-As-You-Earn (CAYE) scheme to help SEPs with their MediSave contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: However, we need to do more and to do better to explain the CPF system to SEPs and encourage or even incentivise them to make contributions so that they can benefit from this national system.

sections.label: Online concert ticket revenue
sections.summary: An online concert ticket cost about S$35, and with hundreds of thousands sold, revenue reached almost S$26 million for one performance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The ticket price for the online concert was about S$35, just 5% of the average price of a BTS concert in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: However, with hundreds of thousands of online tickets sold, the total revenue reached almost S$26 million, just for one performance.

sections.label: Government, reserves and compassion
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government is not family, notes appeals based on friends receiving aid, and describes reserves as reservoirs of care and compassion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Government is not our spouse, not our parents, not our children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: I have also received some appeals for financial assistance for the various schemes under the four Budgets on the basis because their friends got it, not because they are in financial difficulties and need the money.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Likewise, we should also tap into our own reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Our reserves are not just our personal savings; but our reserves are our reservoirs of concern and care for our family and loved ones, compassion and empathy for others, especially the more vulnerable, and the mental strength to overcome adversity.

sections.label: Meritocracy in Singapore
sections.summary: Meritocracy, defined as advancement based on individual capabilities and merits, has served Singapore well as a fundamental principle for over 50 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Meritocracy, which can be defined as “a social system in which advancement in society is based on an individual's capabilities and merits” has served Singapore well as a fundamental principle for the past 50-odd years.

sections.label: PSLE grades and merit
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to combine coursework and PSLE scores for a Primary 6 final grade and to broaden the definition of merit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that it is a sorting mechanism for Secondary school placement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, just as almost every Primary school has a combination of coursework and examinations that determine their pupils’ year-end grades for each Primary level from Primary 1 to Primary 5, I strongly urge the MOE to see how they can make each Primary 6 student’s grade a final grade, a combination of coursework and their PSLE examination score.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And we are living in a world where it is increasingly not so much about what you know any more; rather, it is about what you can do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I would hope that the MOE can examine the methodology of allocating a final grade to all Primary 6 students that is based on a combination of school-based coursework and the standard PSLE examination, instead of all students being simply reduced to a one-shot, high-pressure, examination-based mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And while we aspire to move beyond examination-based academics, why not challenge ourselves to go beyond academics altogether as we broaden the definition of “merit” to redefine what “excellence” should look like.

sections.label: Impactful Singaporean athletes
sections.summary: The speaker cites powerlifter Irving Henson, who broke a world record, and indoor skydiver Kyra Poh as athletes who made an impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In sport, for example, let us pop our heads out of the pool for a second and look at athletes who have made an impact, such as Irving Henson, the Singaporean Powerlifter who broke the world record, and the indoor skydiving phenomenon that is Kyra Poh.

sections.label: More arts scholarships and bursaries
sections.summary: A call for more arts scholarships and bursaries, including in non-traditional fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Let us have more arts scholarships and bursaries, not just for the traditional fields, but in other non-traditional fields, too.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Conversations dialogues
sections.summary: The Government intends to convene Emerging Stronger Conversations for Singaporeans to hold dialogues on societal issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But, perhaps, these are the parts of our community that we have not always heard, engaged or connected with, and who are somehow feeling more like a discarded scrap of cloth, rather than part of a beautiful and wonderful quilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, it heartens me to note that the Government is intending to convene the Emerging Stronger Conversations so that all Singaporeans can have meaningful dialogues about important societal issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These conversations, Mdm Deputy Speaker, have the potential to be the stitching that will reinforce and strengthen the parts of the quilt – but only if we are able to take a long, hard honest look at ourselves and have the difficult conversations that need to be had.

sections.label: Conversations and Singapore's future
sections.summary: The speaker fears Singapore is finished otherwise, but is confident respectful conversations will craft a better Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And if that should happen, then I fear that Singapore is finished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But if we come together in these conversations and treat each other with dignity and respect, then I am confident that not only will we mend these tears, but – working together – we will all craft a better Singapore quilt, a stronger Singapore quilt, one that will provide warmth, comfort and security for many generations to come.

sections.label: Workplace success beyond academic results
sections.summary: Academic results offer a first step into careers, but interpersonal skills, attitude, commitment, drive and leadership lead to promotion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some despair when they realise that success in real life takes time and endurance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I often remind parents in Edusave ceremonies that in their workplace, their colleagues get promoted not based on academic results.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Academic results offer that first step into their careers but then, it is their interpersonal skills, attitude at work, such as commitment, drive and leadership skills, that lead to promotion.

sections.label: Friend's salary rise over ten years
sections.summary: A friend who was an administrative clerk earning $1,600 was earning $12,000 ten years later.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Both became very useful in my later career.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I also remember chatting with my friend, then an administrative clerk earning $1,600, wondering how we would ever be able to afford a flat.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Ten years on, she was earning a more than comfortable $12,000.

sections.label: Concern over asking Government for money
sections.summary: Government money has given reprieve from hardships, but the speaker is concerned some may keep asking for more.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The money from the Government has given them some reprieve from severe hardships and difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that some people may be tempted to keep asking the Government for more money, even if they can survive with some sacrifices.

sections.label: Retired flat owners seek more money
sections.summary: Retired flat owners refused to downgrade or do a lease buy-back and asked the Government for more money, which the speaker calls a cause for concern.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, they refused to downgrade or right-size or do a lease buy-back of their paid-up flat in case they wanted to leave their flat to their children in spite of all this.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: They were retired and asked the Government to give them more money.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: While these cases are few, it is, nevertheless, a cause for concern if more people think like them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As the Finance Minister has explained, we need to use the money wisely, to save for real rainy days, and we are in the middle of a very long and heavy thunderstorm right now.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I would go further and urge that we look for ways to cut back on spending, and reduce Ministries' budgets.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Now is the time for all of us to be resilient and work together to restore our financial health, even as we battle the virus to restore our physical health.
